name: entities_are_strings
rationale: The label lower-cases every entity, so a correct output can only contain strings. This catches outputs whose lists hold numbers, nested objects or nulls.

name: entities_nonempty
rationale: Gold entities are non-empty substrings of the text. This catches entries that are empty or contain only whitespace.

name: substring_case_insensitive
rationale: Every gold entity is an exact substring of the text, and the label compares lower-cased values. So every correct entity is a case-insensitive substring of the text. This catches invented or paraphrased entities.

name: token_aligned
rationale: CoNLL entities are spans of whole tokens, so a correct entity must match a contiguous token sequence of the text (case-insensitive). This catches partial-token extractions.

name: entity_has_letter
rationale: Named entities contain letters. This catches numbers, scores and dates extracted as entities, such as "1", "0-0" and "1996-08-26".

name: entity_capitalized_in_text
rationale: Named entities in CoNLL contain at least one uppercase character where they occur in the text. The check accepts if any occurrence qualifies. It catches common-noun phrases like "wild card", "former president" and "world record".

name: count_le_occurrences
rationale: Each gold entity is a distinct span of the text. So an entity string cannot appear across all fields more times than it occurs in the text. This catches the same span being duplicated or assigned to several types.

name: no_punct_edges
rationale: CoNLL entity spans never start or end with a standalone punctuation token. This catches sloppy spans like "( Hungary" or "Reuters .".

name: no_quote_paren_tokens_inside
rationale: Standalone quote or parenthesis tokens never occur inside CoNLL entity spans. This catches spans that run across brackets or quotes.

name: no_leading_lowercase_article
rationale: CoNLL spans exclude a lowercase leading "the", "a" or "an" (for example "the Dodgers" is gold "Dodgers"). The check only rejects when every text occurrence starts with the lowercase article.

name: no_trailing_function_word
rationale: Entity spans do not end with lowercase function words or the possessive "'s" token. This catches over-extended spans like "Malawi 's".

name: max_entity_length
rationale: CoNLL entities are short, essentially always 12 tokens or fewer. This catches whole clauses extracted as a single entity.

name: total_le_capitalized_tokens
rationale: Each gold entity is a non-overlapping span containing at least one token with an uppercase letter. So the total entity count cannot exceed the number of such tokens. This catches over-generation.

name: no_weekday_entity
rationale: CoNLL does not tag days of the week. This catches "Monday" or "Saturday" extracted as an entity.

name: no_pronoun_title_entity
rationale: Pronouns and bare titles are never CoNLL entities on their own. This catches entries like "He", "President" or "Minister".

name: no_currency_percent
rationale: Monetary amounts and percentages are not named entities. This catches spans containing "$" or "%".

name: no_date_pattern
rationale: CoNLL does not tag dates. This catches strings like "1996-08-26" or "08/26/96".

name: no_score_token
rationale: Score tokens like "0-0" or "13-10" are never part of an entity. This catches score extraction.

name: lowercase_text_empty
rationale: If the text has no uppercase letter at all, it contains no capitalized named entity. So every field must be empty, and any extraction is rejected.

name: no_clause_punct_inside
rationale: Entity spans never contain standalone ";", "?", "!" or ":" tokens. This catches spans that cross clause boundaries.

name: no_irregular_whitespace
rationale: Gold entities are substrings of single-space-tokenized text, so their internal whitespace is single spaces. This catches tabs, newlines or double spaces inside an entity.

name: list_len_le_tokens
rationale: Non-overlapping spans cannot outnumber the tokens of the text. This catches runaway lists in any field.

name: no_time_token
rationale: Clock times are not named entities. This catches tokens like "10:30", "GMT 1430" style pieces, or "a.m." / "p.m." inside an entity.

name: no_all_lowercase_multiword_else
rationale: A multi-word "else" entry where every text occurrence is fully lowercase cannot be a named entity. This specifically catches phrases like "alien-led profit boost".

name: no_number_only_token_edges
rationale: Entity spans essentially never end with a pure-number token, so a trailing number signals an over-extended span (for example "Hungary 1"). Leading numbers are allowed because names like "1860 Munich" exist.
